the project aims to provide effective and sustainable management of the park and its surrounding buffer zone which will provide overall benefits in terms of biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services. It would also facilitate socio-economic benefits for communities living near the forest through co-management and sustainable production of raw materials and Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs). A standard process will be followed in each of the pilot sites, starting with a detailed diagnosis involving all stakeholders to confirm the ecological values and vocations of the site as a territory, the main threats to biodiversity, and the opportunities in terms of socio-economic activities and partnerships. If the site has already been the subject of a support project or the development of specific socio-economic activities, feedback will enable lessons to be drawn and success factors to be identified. Based on the approved diagnosis, the participatory process will go on to define the various components of the management plan. This exercise will make it possible to determine the most appropriate governance and management model, following the proposals drawn up as part of additional study no. 3 conducted during the project appraisal. Furthermore, the projects aims to engage International experts who will provide guidance on fostering meaningful engagement of local communities and other stakeholders in protected area management decision-making processes, promoting collaborative conservation initiatives and socio-economic benefit sharing. The project will build on ongoing projects and will support the National Parks in the implementation of a robust ecological and socio-economic monitoring system. Moreover, ecotourism will be supported as an instrument to reinforce protected areas management.
